Randolph High School 1970 Yearbook Photo A homicide victim whose skeletal remains were found in a shallow grave in a wooded area of Quincy 35 years ago has been identified with the help of advanced DNA technology and forensic genetic genealogy, the Norfolk district attorney’s office said Friday. 
 Now, investigators are asking for the public’s help figuring out who killed Glenn Powers, a 1970 graduate of Randolph High School. 
 The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner determined that Powers was killed by blunt force trauma, prosecutors said. 
 Neither Powers’ date of birth, nor his age at the time of his killing, were disclosed. 
 A hiker spotted the remains in the vicinity of 270 Quarry St. on March 21, 1991. The Patriot Ledger reported at the time that the body had been there at least six months. 
 The now developed site is near the Sergeant Robert Allen Curry/Michael G. Therrien Fields. 
 “We never forget a victim, no matter how much time goes by,” Norfolk District Attorney Michael W. Morrissey said in a statement Friday. 
 “The District Attorney’s Office and our local police partners do not refer to unsolved crimes as ‘cold cases,’” Morrissey said. “Every victim deserves justice and our office is committed to bringing some measure of closure to the families of the victims.” 
 Now that Powers has been identified, Morrissey said it is time to focus on solving his murder. He asked the public to help. 
 “In this case, we are committed to searching for Glenn’s killer or killers and holding them accountable,” Morrissey said. “We are appealing to the public for help. Someone knows what happened to Glenn or knows information that may help to identify who is responsible for his murder.” 
 To identify Powers, investigators used a method that combines DNA sequencing with traditional family tree research found in public online databases and public records, Morrissey’s office said. 
 The Ramapo College of New Jersey Investigative Genetic Genealogy Center performed the genealogical research, and the Massachusetts State Police Crime Lab, along with BODE Technology, conducted the DNA analysis. 
 Investigators urge anyone with information about the homicide to contact the MSP tip line at the Norfolk district attorney’s office, 781-830-4990, or Quincy Police at 617-745-5768, or the Massachusetts State Police Unresolved Case Unit at 1-855-MA-SOLVE or 1-855-627-6583.
